description.value: The Gold River branch of the Vancouver Island Regional Library is a small public library situated on the unceded traditional territory of the Mowachaht and Muchalaht First Nations, first opened in 1967 and operating at its current location since December 1992. It is one of the few public amenities in this remote Vancouver Island community and offers free WiFi and public computers to all visitors. For touring cyclists moving through Gold River, it serves as a connectivity and rest point in a town with limited services.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website branch page confirms 'Free public WiFi' under Branch Features, directly corroborating OSM tags internet_access=wlan and internet_access:fee=no. The branch page lists only printing/photocopying, two public computers, free WiFi, holds pickup, 24/7 bookdrop, and grab-and-go bags — no mention of bike parking, washrooms, or water refill, so all required criteria remain null. The website URL resolves to the correct branch page confirming the OSM website tag, but no phone number or street address appears in the retrieved content to cross-check those OSM fields.
concerns: Required criteria for bike parking, washrooms, and water refill are all unconfirmed — the branch page's feature list does not mention any of these.
Phone number and street address could not be verified from the retrieved website content.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: All three required criteria (bike parking, washrooms, water refill) are unconfirmed from available evidence. A public library with free WiFi in a remote community has clear utility for touring cyclists, but cannot be included without confirming at least the required criteria.

wow_evidence: Small remote branch; ordinary library band.
blurb: Gold River's small library, one of the town's few public amenities.
